newsitem.title: USA: Rubbermaid on track with realignment plan.
newsitem.headline: Rubbermaid on track with realignment plan.

text.p: Rubbermaid Inc said on Wednesday it is "on track" to achieve savings targeted in its two-year realignment plan.

The company said when it completes its restructuring at the end of calendar year 1997, it would have a running rate of savings of $50 million a year. Rubbermaid pointed to its current cash flow figures as an indication of the changes taking place at the company.

"Our improvement in operating cash flow indicates that we are making progress in our strategies to become a low-cost producer while maintaining innovation leadership in our chosen markets," said Rubbermaid's chairman and chief executive, Wolfgang Schmitt.
Rubbermaid posted $315-million cash flow from operations in 1996, up $85 million over the prior year.

"We have met the goal we set early in 1994 to achieve $335 million in productivity savings. Furthermore, we accelerated changes with our two-year realignment plan, and we are on target to achieve improvements outlined in that plan," Schmitt said.

The company said it reduced its stock-keeping units, or SKUs, by 45 percent in the first half of 1996 in order to simplify logistics and inventory management. It also moved out of two million square feet of leased warehouse space and has plans to eliminate two million more square feet of space.

The company posted fourth-quarter earnings were $152.4 million, or $1.01 per share, compared with 1995 net earnings of $59.8 million, or $0.38 per share. Net sales in 1996 were $2.36 billion, compared with $2.34 billion a year ago.
Schmitt said the second half of the year was more difficult than the first because of further increases in plastic resin costs and a more competitive pricing stance.
On average for various plastic resins used by Rubbermaid, costs rose 40 percent from the first quarter to the fourth quarter of 1996, the consumer products company said.
